sections.h2: Does a listing or a cash sale fit a Durham owner better?
sections.html:
Listing is built for the highest price, and cash is built for speed and a shorter to-do list. Durham owners holding an inherited, tenant-occupied or tired house often get both numbers before choosing.

Renters make up a large share of the city. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures show 52.3 percent of homes lived in by their owners, so nearly half of households rent, and a landlord may bid as readily as a family.

  • Agent listing: a good match when the house shows well and you can sit through inspections and underwriting.
  • Sale by owner: workable if you can set a price and handle the contract.
  • Cash purchase: useful when repairs, tenants, probate or a date make a long listing impractical.

The deed is filed in Durham County, and the statutes rank rival conveyances by the time each was registered.

sections.h2: What do federal figures show about Durham's housing and residents?
sections.html:
A mid-2025 estimate puts Durham at 305,561 people, compared with 283,506 counted in 2020 and 228,330 in 2010, spread over 112.79 square miles of land.

Medicine dominates the business data: QuickFacts shows 6,106,797 thousand dollars of 2022 receipts for health care and social assistance, versus 1,277,689 thousand dollars for lodging and food. A bachelor's degree or higher belongs to 57.3 percent of adults past 25, and a typical commute takes 22.3 minutes.

sections.h2: When does Durham County reappraise, and what comes next?
sections.html:
Values now in force date from January 1, 2025, and the county lists January 1, 2029 as the next reappraisal. Under state law every county must reappraise within eight years, though commissioners can pull the date forward by resolution.

The county says a long gap in a fast-growing place breeds large, unpredictable swings, which is why it shortened its cycle. Between reappraisals a parcel's value can still change through new construction, rezoning or a split. Then the county uses the last cycle's rates: a house built in 2026 on land that was vacant in 2025 is appraised at January 1, 2025 prices, in the county's own example.

  • The office values at full fair market value as of the effective date.
  • Appraising and taxing are separate steps, and each jurisdiction picks its own rate.
  • Measurements come from the outside, so square footage can differ from a fee appraisal.

Buying a new build? The county's advice is to have the closing attorney estimate tax from the price, which gives a rough figure and not the bill itself.

sections.h2: How do I dispute my Durham County value?
sections.html:
File in the county's Tax Help portal, the method it recommends, or on a paper form, ahead of the Board of Equalization and Review's adjournment. A change-of-value notice instead opens a window of 30 days. The county's call center, 919-560-0300, can mail a form.

Adjournment is announced in the Durham Herald-Sun and on the county site. The 2025 cutoff was June 16 at 5:00 p.m., long gone, so follow the current year's notice. A review runs 30 to 120 days, and the county rules out affordability and the size of a bill increase as grounds.

  • Bring comparable sales: for the 2025 cycle the county looked at 2023 and 2024 sales and excluded related-party deals, foreclosures, short sales and auctions.
  • A fee appraisal or closing statement from near the effective date can help, though a single sale may not show the typical price.
  • Relief is prospective: G.S. 105-287 says a lowered value is not retroactive.

Five residents sit on the board, each named by a different county commissioner. You may attend, but the board will rule on your papers if you cannot. Beyond the board lies the state Property Tax Commission, reached within a month of the board's mailed decision.

sections.h2: Who can file if an heir or a company holds title?
sections.html:
For a person's home, the owner, an attorney licensed in North Carolina or a holder of power of attorney may file, yet only the owner or a lawyer may argue at the hearing. The county treats its board as quasi-judicial, so advocacy there can amount to practicing law.

Entities have a narrower list: a lawyer, an officer, an LLC manager, an authorized W-2 employee, or an owner holding at least a quarter of the company. All but the lawyer file a non-attorney representative form, and an agent under power of attorney may not file for an entity.

Selling an inherited house? Check who held title on January 1, because the county fixes ownership annually on that date. Forward any notice that reaches you after a sale.

sections.h2: What relief programs can a Durham owner use?
sections.html:
Three state programs exist, and each owner picks a single one. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor.

  • Older or disabled owners: an exclusion of at least $25,000, tied to a 2026 income cap NCDOR prints as $38,800.
  • Disabled veterans: $45,000 of value, and the form shows no age or income cap.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is held to a share of income, and the difference is deferred as a lien.

The county's FAQ also describes present-use treatment for farmland and woodland. Agriculture needs a 10 acre tract in production, horticulture needs 5 acres, and forestry needs 20 acres, with a $1,000 average gross income test over three years for the first two. QuickFacts counts 11,287 Durham veterans, so the veteran exclusion deserves a look.

sections.h2: What does a Durham seller pay for the deed tax and recording?
sections.html:
Sellers owe deed excise tax at the Register of Deeds before filing: a dollar for every $500 of price, remainder rounded up. Half stays with the county and half goes to the state.

Recording uses one statewide fee schedule. An ordinary instrument costs $26.00 through 15 pages plus $4.00 for each later page, a deed of trust costs $64.00 through 35 pages, and a certified copy runs $5.00 for page one and $2.00 per extra page.

Because the year's tax lien reaches back to the January listing date, ask the closing attorney to confirm with Durham County that the bill is paid or arranged before funds move.

sections.h2: Which Durham zoning and landlord rules matter before selling?
sections.html:
Durham's Unified Development Ordinance allows one accessory dwelling per lot. Heated floor area may reach 1,000 square feet for a single story and 1,200 square feet overall, with a different cap in the rural district. Check with planning staff on your lot before you promise a backyard unit to anyone.

  • Tenants: a monthly tenancy ends on a week's notice, and unpaid rent can end a lease 10 days after demand.
  • Foreclosure: heard by the superior court clerk, with later bids required to top the last by 5 percent, minimum $750.
  • Probate: an affidavit can settle an intestate estate of $20,000 or less once 30 days have passed, and no state estate tax applies to recent deaths.

Hand a buyer the lease and the permit file for any work on the house.

faqs.q: Which government values and taxes a Durham house?
faqs.a: Durham County does both, and every taxing body sets its own rate, so the final bill waits on those rates.

faqs.q: What is the next Durham County reappraisal date?
faqs.a: The county lists January 1, 2029. The current set of values began January 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Will a lowered value earn me a refund for past years?
faqs.a: No. State law makes a reduction effective for the year it is made and never retroactive.

faqs.q: How long does a Durham appeal review run?
faqs.a: The county says 30 to 120 days, depending on how many appeals your neighborhood produces.

faqs.q: Must I be home when a county appraiser visits?
faqs.a: Only if the appraiser needs to see the interior. Measurements are taken outside, and an appointment is set first if access is needed.
